Quito: church vaults and altar with gold-toned decoration

Visit to Quilotoa Crater Lake

Duration of the sightseeing day, including transfers: about 11 hours.
Transfers: Quito to Quilotoa (3.5 hours), Quilotoa to Baños (3.5 hours).
Maximum elevation on the route: 3,900 m above sea level.
Overnight elevation: 1,800 m above sea level.

Average temperature during the outing: around +10 °C.

After breakfast, we continue to Quilotoa Crater Lake, one of Ecuador's most striking natural sights. On the way, we'll visit an artisan's workshop in the village of Tigua, where the well-known style of naïve painting originated. Local artists paint bright scenes of the Andean landscape, traditionally on sheepskin.

We then travel through Ecuador's scenic Central Andes along the well-known Pujilí road to the village of Quilotoa.

On arrival, we'll stop at a viewpoint overlooking the emerald crater lake inside an extinct volcano. You'll also have the chance to walk through an Indigenous community and learn about local life.

If the group wishes, you can walk down to the lakeshore, go kayaking and ride a mule back up. Kayak hire and mule rides cost extra. Local residents offer mule rides on an informal basis, and the service is generally available until around 15:00.

Main stops: viewpoints, the Tigua painting gallery and Quilotoa Crater Lake.

After the visit, we transfer to Baños and check in at the hotel. The evening is free.

Accommodation: 4-star Sangay Hotel.

Meals: breakfast and a boxed lunch.
